hook: The sunlight on your skin left the Sun about eight minutes ago.

blocks.narration: The sunlight on your skin left the Sun about eight minutes ago. But the energy behind it is thousands of years old.
blocks.visual: Cinematic 3D render of sunlight streaming through clouds onto a person's open hand, glowing accents

blocks.narration: Light from the Sun's surface takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to cross one hundred fifty million kilometers to Earth.
blocks.visual: A beam of light races across black space from a blazing Sun toward a small blue Earth

blocks.narration: But that light starts much deeper, in the core, where hydrogen fuses into helium at around fifteen million degrees Celsius.
blocks.visual: Camera dives into the Sun, through glowing layers to a white-hot pulsing core

blocks.narration: The core is so dense that energy cannot travel straight out. It is absorbed and re-emitted over and over in random directions.
blocks.visual: A tiny glowing particle bounces chaotically in a dense sea of plasma

blocks.narration: Scientists call this a random walk. Each step goes a tiny distance in a random direction, so progress outward is painfully slow.
blocks.visual: A zig-zag path traced in light winds slowly outward through the layers

blocks.narration: Estimates say this journey takes somewhere between ten thousand and one hundred seventy thousand years to reach the surface.
blocks.visual: A timeline stretches across ancient eras, from early human cave fires to modern cities

blocks.narration: Then, once it finally escapes, the last leg to your face takes just over eight minutes. The slow part is inside the Sun.
blocks.visual: Light bursts free from the Sun's surface and streaks toward Earth in seconds

blocks.narration: Every sunny day, you are literally warmed by ancient energy. Follow for one space fact that breaks your brain each day.
blocks.visual: Golden hour sunlight on a calm ocean as the camera slowly pulls back

captions.body: Light from the Sun's surface reaches Earth in about 8 minutes 20 seconds. But energy made by fusion in the core takes an estimated 10,000 to 170,000 years to work its way out to the surface.

youtube_title: The Sunlight Hitting You Is Older Than Civilization
